summary: Independent GRAVEYARD expectations/execution pass covered all 12 active-batch companies using the latest available market close before this premarket cycle plus current primary operating evidence. Earth Score remains untouched and no pre-T0 Action State is published. Expectation risk remains highest where valuation requires sustained AI-cycle continuation despite concentration or execution blockers; MU remains the clearest case where a low-looking forward multiple can be deceptive because current earnings may be near a scarcity-cycle extreme.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Valuation still assumes years of successful launch/space-systems scaling and Neutron execution; strong backlog does not eliminate schedule/dilution sensitivity.
contradictions: Operating momentum is strong while valuation leaves little room for program failure.
unknowns: Normalized 3-5 year FCF margin and diluted share count.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Neutron and backlog conversion scale without material dilution while margins improve.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Rapid growth/profitability support premium valuation, but current expectations implicitly assume concentrated hyperscaler demand remains durable rather than cliff-like.
contradictions: Exceptional growth coexists with extreme end-customer concentration.
unknowns: Independent consensus revisions and normalized duration economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Revenue diversifies materially while high growth/margins persist.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Valuation requires Scorpio and connectivity ramps to convert into broad, durable platform revenue; high margins alone do not remove product-transition risk.
contradictions: Quality economics coexist with ramp/customer concentration.
unknowns: Current end-customer concentration and long-run operating margin after portfolio expansion.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Scorpio broadens customer base and sustains operating leverage.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Massive market value embeds extraordinary durability of AI infrastructure spend, platform share and margins; policy/customer concentration makes the expectation bar unusually high.
contradictions: Primary evidence supports exceptional demand but not immunity from custom accelerators/export controls.
unknowns: Reproducible terminal margin and displacement assumptions.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: NVIDIA sustains share/margins while broadening demand beyond a small CSP set.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Premium valuation requires continued accelerator scaling and CPU share gains against NVIDIA/custom silicon; strong data-center growth is necessary but not sufficient.
contradictions: Growth is real while durable accelerator economics remain less proven.
unknowns: Normalized accelerator margin and independent customer breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Instinct converts design wins into broad repeat deployments with expanding margin.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Very high absolute valuation is supported by exceptional FCF and custom-AI/networking growth; risk is more about program concentration/project durability than simple multiple optics.
contradictions: Cash generation is strong while a few customers can still dominate incremental AI economics.
unknowns: Customer-specific AI margins and normalized growth after current megaproject ramp.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI customer diversification and software cash flow sustain growth while leverage falls.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Valuation reflects leading-edge scarcity and assumes geopolitical/overseas-fab risks remain manageable; ordinary earnings multiples understate tail risk.
contradictions: Foundry leadership coexists with concentrated physical geography.
unknowns: Market-implied Taiwan risk premium and normalized overseas-fab margin drag.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Geographic diversification scales without major margin dilution while node leadership persists.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Premium valuation assumes EUV/High-NA scarcity and AI-led fab expansion persist; policy/customer capex cycles remain asymmetric downside channels.
contradictions: Backlog visibility coexists with export-policy sensitivity.
unknowns: Current geographic mix and customer High-NA utilization economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: High-NA adoption accelerates with resilient backlog through capex normalization.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: ARM retains one of the highest expectation burdens: valuation prices major royalty expansion into AI/data center while filing evidence still shows concentrated customers/control relationships.
contradictions: Asset-light economics are exceptional but do not remove customer/Arm China/SoftBank dependence.
unknowns: How much future server/AI economics are contracted versus aspirational TAM.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Royalty/CSS economics compound much faster while concentration declines.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Headline forward valuation can look cheap because HBM/memory earnings are extraordinary; normalized mid-cycle economics matter more than current multiple.
contradictions: Strategic agreements improve visibility while memory remains cyclical/supply-responsive.
unknowns: Normalized mid-cycle HBM/DRAM margin after capacity response.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Customer agreements and HBM leadership keep margins structurally above historical cycle norms.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Premium multiple requires AI networking growth and exceptional margins to persist; common hyperscaler capex dependence makes timing sensitive.
contradictions: Strong balance sheet supports quality while customer/architecture concentration remains strategic.
unknowns: Current top-customer shares and independent buyer breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: AI networking diversifies across customers while margins remain durable.

perCompanyCoverage.expectationTest: Valuation assumes AI power/cooling scarcity converts into durable high-margin backlog; execution hinges on conversion quality, not raw order growth.
contradictions: Backlog supports demand while power/interconnection delays can defer realization.
unknowns: Current cancellation terms, backlog aging and normalized TTM margin.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Backlog converts on schedule with sustained price-cost and broader customer mix.

materialFindings.finding: Latest market close remains the appropriate reproducible market snapshot for this premarket GRAVEYARD cycle; no intraday precision is fabricated.
ARM, RKLB, ALAB, CRDO, AMD and ANET retain especially high expectation sensitivity because current valuation requires strong continuation while key concentration/execution blockers remain unresolved.
MU remains a peak-cycle normalization problem rather than a simple cheap-multiple opportunity; current earnings can make forward valuation optically low.

contradictions: Strong Earth-quality operating evidence and elevated market expectations coexist; neither overwrites the other.
Low forward multiples can be misleading when earnings are near cyclical/scarcity peaks.
unknowns: No official pre-T0 Action State or Execution Score is warranted.
Defensible bear/base/bull per-share ranges remain blocked by incomplete normalized share counts, cash/debt and long-run margins for multiple batch names.
Secondary analyst consensus is not treated as canonical evidence.

peerRequests.request: Complete normalized diluted-share counts, cash/debt and mid-cycle margin assumptions before any formal per-share valuation bridge.
Identify which batch companies retain economics under an AI-capex downshift versus those mainly participating in the same spending wave.

accuracyDebates.reason: Prevents MU-like cyclical peaks from being misread as low expectation risk.
Market data must not silently create rank/action authority before T0.
